description: The report Python prints for an unhandled exception: read it from the last line, which names the type and message, up through the calls that led there.
`raise ValueError("message")` stops the function and sends the exception to the caller; a bare `raise` inside `except` re-raises the current one.
Runs a block and handles the exceptions whose type matches a clause; a tuple such as `except (ValueError, TypeError):` handles several.
`else` runs only when the `try` block raised nothing; `finally` runs in every case, even after `return` or an unhandled exception.
`except Exception:` or a bare `except:` also swallows bugs; catch the specific types you know how to handle.
